A PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md file in GitHub provides a predefined format that developers fill out when creating a Pull Request (PR).
It helps maintainers understand what changes were made and why.
It usually includes:
- Description: What changes were made?
- Related issues: Which issue does this PR fix?
- Testing: How were the changes tested?
- Checklist: Have coding guidelines been followed?
Example:
## Description
Describe your changes here.

## Related Issue
Fixes #123

## Testing
How did you test your changes?

## Checklist
- [ ] Code tested
- [ ] Documentation updated


In short:
- README.md → What the project is about.
- CONTRIBUTING.md → How to contribute.
- PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md → What information to include when submitting code changes.
GitHub can automatically show this template when someone opens a new pull request.
